request.text: You are an expert reviewer of a CLI configuration-architecture proposal. Read the proposal below (a real design for the `agents-cli` tool at /home/muqsit/src/github.com/muqsitnawaz/agents-cli — you may inspect the repo, especially cli/src/lib/types.ts, cli/src/commands/setup.ts, cli/src/commands/rules.ts, cli/docs/resources.md, and ~/.agents/.system/). Give SHARP, SPECIFIC feedback. Do not rubber-stamp. Answer the 5 critique questions at the end directly, and add any design risk the proposal misses. Keep it under 500 words. Ground claims in file:line where possible. Return plain prose, no preamble. PROPOSAL: # Proposal: make `.agents` a neutral, per-target configuration ## Problem `agents setup` clones an opinionated system repo (`gh:phnx-labs/.agents-system`, `types.ts:475`) into `~/.agents/.system/` as the lowest resolution layer. Everyone who installs the CLI inherits: - the author's mission/workflow **rules** (one flat `default` preset, `rules/rules.yaml`), - **hooks** that auto-run (`agents.yaml` hooks manifest), - **plugins** (already inert until enabled — good). Two distinct asks: 1. **De-opinionate** so the CLI is reusable by others (neutral engine, bring-your-own opinions). 2. **Per-target applicability** — a rule or hook should be enable-able/disable-able per model (harness) and per device, because Fable 5.1 ≠ GPT Astra in personality. ## Key finding: the mechanism half-exists and was abandoned From `cli/src/lib/types.ts`: - `Manifest` (agents.yaml) already has `agents?: Partial<Record<AgentId,string>>` — but only used for version pins. - `ManifestHook.enabled?: boolean` — per-hook disable ALREADY works at user layer. - `ManifestHook.agents?: AgentId[]` — **`@deprecated ... field is ignored`**. Per-harness hook targeting existed, got ripped out; coverage is now hardcoded per-event in `hooks.ts`. - Rules: single flat `default` preset, no per-harness overlay. So we generalize the targeting that was half-built, do it *right* (resolver-honored, not ignored), and unify it across rules + hooks. ## Proposal ### A. Neutral default (de-opinionate) - Flip `DEFAULT_SYSTEM_REPO` so a fresh setup clones **nothing** (or a tiny public `agents-starter` skeleton = base rules only). Prompt: "point at a system repo? (optional)". - Author's `.agents-system` becomes a repo you *opt into* via `AGENTS_SYSTEM_REPO`, same as any reuser. - Confidential mission/Prix rules move OUT of any cloneable system repo, into the **user layer** only. - Hooks from a shared layer land **inert** (`enabled: false`) with a printed `agents hooks enable <name>`. ### B. One applicability model across all resources Every resource (rule subrule, hook, plugin, command) may carry an optional selector: ```yaml when: agents: [codex, grok]      # only these harnesses devices: [zion]            # only these machines not: { agents: [claude] }  # everywhere except ``` Absent `when:` = applies everywhere (the neutral default). Resolved by the ONE resolver, honored at sync/registration. This resurrects the deprecated `agents:` field, correctly, and is the single answer to "enable/disable a rule or hook per model." ### C. Rules: base + per-harness overlays (compose, don't fork) ```yaml presets: default: subrules: [foundations, code-quality, testing-strict, ...]   # base (harness-neutral) overlays: codex: [codex-terse-no-preamble]      # thin deltas, layered on top of base grok:  [grok-directness] ``` Resolution = base ∪ overlay(activeHarness). Small reason-giving deltas, never a full per-model AGENTS.md fork. Overlay content is decided EMPIRICALLY from `agents insights` failure modes, not Twitter vibes. ### D. Device scoping — the `devices/` idea `agents.yaml` at top level = shared/default. Machine-specific choices layer via: ``` .agents/ agents.yaml            # shared defaults (all devices) devices/ default.yaml         # fallback per-device overrides zion.yaml            # this hostname wins on zion ``` Resolution order becomes: project > devices/<hostname> > devices/default > user > extra > system. This is the existing layered resolver, extended by one device axis. Top-level stays for truly shared config; per-machine (which accounts/harnesses exist here) goes under `devices/`. ### E. Onboarding / the "re-choose on every account add" problem Root cause: today "which resources sync" is coupled to "which account/harness you just added". Fix — decouple into declarative **policy** vs. **accounts**: - Onboarding writes a sync **policy** ONCE into the manifest: "these resource sets apply to these harness classes." - Adding an account/harness later is a **no-prompt** operation: the new harness inherits policy automatically. - Only prompt when the new harness matches NO policy — offer {apply default / customize once}, then remember it. So the manifest (`agents.yaml` + `devices/`) is the durable source of truth; onboarding writes it, account-adds read it. ## Before / After summary - BEFORE: clone opinionated repo → flat rules for all models → hooks auto-run everywhere → re-choose sync per account. - AFTER: neutral engine → base+overlay rules with `when:` targeting → hooks inert + per-target → policy chosen once, accounts inherit. ## Rules removed vs kept (from current `default` preset) Confidential/personal (move to user layer, OUT of shared): mission (Prix), tech-stack, feed-status-posts, remote-fleet-dispatch, conventions (getrush-specific), agents-cli-repo-specific. Keep as neutral base: foundations, research-discipline, code-quality, testing-strict, truly-agentic-git-workflow, gh-merge-guard, no-pr-footer, plan-presentation, task-checklists, ui-work-discipline. ## Critique questions for reviewers 1. Is the single `when:` selector the right unification, or should hooks vs rules stay separate? 2. Device scoping via `devices/<hostname>.yaml` — right axis, or does it explode the resolution matrix? 3. The policy-vs-accounts decoupling for onboarding — does it actually remove the re-prompt, or move it? 4. Base+overlay for rules — will overlays drift/rot vs one file? Better alternative? 5. What breaks for existing users of the current `.agents-system` when the default goes neutral?
